html:
Quinoa is a grain-like seed grown on the high plains of the Andes, around Lake Titicaca and the salt flats of southern Bolivia. It was domesticated thousands of years ago and was a staple of Andean peoples.

It grows where little else can, in cold, dry and salty soils. It was a main food in Tiwanaku and the Inca world. After the conquest, Spanish wheat and barley pushed it aside, and for centuries it was seen as the food of the poor.

From the 2000s demand from health-food buyers in North America and Europe made quinoa a booming export, and the UN named 2013 the International Year of Quinoa. Prices rose, and farmers around the Uyuni salt flat in Bolivia planted far more, which raised worries about soil. It has also become a symbol of Andean food, alongside the potato.
